stubsRequiredForBitIdentity.performanceNow: REQUIRED. Sole time authority of the loop (update() takes no argument). Stub to a virtual clock advancing a fixed 16.667ms per step. Prior session (P15-1 wetness A/B) achieved dye+velocity bit-identity with exactly this technique.
stubsRequiredForBitIdentity.requestAnimationFrame: REQUIRED while manually stepping. update() unconditionally re-arms rAF (js/05j-update-loop.js:1337); replace window.requestAnimationFrame with a callback-swallowing stub before calling window.update() yourself, or real vsync ticks double-step the sim. Note the rAF stub must be installed AFTER boot completes (or be pass-through during boot): the deferred UI build and boot choreography need real rAF (see memory: hidden-tab rAF pause blocks the deferred UI build).
stubsRequiredForBitIdentity.mathRandom: REQUIRED. Pin Math.random to a seeded PRNG (e.g. mulberry32) via Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument or before painting begins — the splat shader stamp seed is fresh random on EVERY dab (js/05i-sim-stats.js:110).
stubsRequiredForBitIdentity.dateNow: NOT required for dye/velocity identity in a solo run: update() and the whole splat path never read Date.now (only a comment at js/05j-update-loop.js:120 mentions it). Date.now is used by recording (js/03-recording.js), multiplayer ids/timers (js/06-multiplayer.js:1800), and animation ids (js/04d-anim-ascend-star.js:205) — stub it too if those features run.
stubsRequiredForBitIdentity.governor: window.QualityGovernor adapts resolution/iterations/fx to measured CPU time, including a boot-time quality ascent that ramps FBO resolution (js/08a-quality-governor.js:44-160; hooks at js/05j-update-loop.js:695-697 effIters, :909-910 fxOn gating MacCormack, js/05c-programs-framebuffers.js:151-152 dyeScale/simScale). Call window.QualityGovernor.setEnabled(false) (js/08a-quality-governor.js:480) before measuring, or two runs can diverge in pressure iterations, MacCormack on/off, and FBO resolution.

manualStepRecipe: 1. Launch app; wait for window.__scriptsReady === true (index.html:1210) and window.Boot frame-done / window.__stats populated (first frame drawn: js/05j-update-loop.js:1333-1336)

2. Wait past the synthetic +1px resize fired 500ms after init (js/05n-hotkeys-init.js:521-532) — it triggers an FBO reinit; wait until no _fboSettleAtMs rebuild is pending (e.g. ~1s of real time), then keep the canvas wrapper size untouched for the whole run
3. window.QualityGovernor.setEnabled(false); window.fpsCap = 0; pin Math.random with a seeded PRNG
4. Swap window.requestAnimationFrame for a no-op stub (swallow the callback), and stub performance.now to a virtual clock

5. Per frame: advance virtual clock by 16.667ms, inject input (window.applyMultiSplatWith(x,y,dx,dy,color,mult,radius,exactColor) — js/05g-arm-colors.js:294 — or drive window.BrushEngine/pointer state), then call window.update()

pauseGates.isPaused: top-level let at js/01-config.js:32 — NOT on window; gates the entire paint+physics block at js/05j-update-loop.js:226 (display/post-FX still run; processReplay still runs, :225). Flipped only by window.togglePause() (js/04f-canvas-actions.js:73-85) and multiplayer state sync (js/06-multiplayer.js:604-606).
pauseGates.visibilityAutoPause: js/04f-canvas-actions.js:149-173 — document.hidden => togglePause() (pausedByVisibility), auto-resume on visible. A hidden/backgrounded tab ALSO stops rAF entirely (browser behavior — the known preview-harness failure mode). Harness options: keep the window visible, or after the visibilitychange fires call window.togglePause() to unpause and drive window.update() manually (manual calls bypass the rAF freeze).

verifiedReadbackCode.byte: RGBA8 stores read with gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE — js/05l-layers-transform.js:758, js/05o-masks.js:88-92 (note: a lost GL context makes readPixels a silent all-zero no-op — both sites guard for it)
verifiedReadbackCode.glAccess: gl is a top-level lexical binding shared across the classic-script chunks; injected page scripts reach it as bare `gl` exactly like js/08b-jank-monitor.js does (guard: typeof gl !== 'undefined', 08b:336)

readback.readFormatNote: readPixels with gl.RGBA / gl.FLOAT returns 4 floats per pixel even for RG16F velocity and R16F pressure targets (extra channels read 0/1); allocate width*height*4 Float32Array

hashRecipe.recommended: Per-checkpoint: read velocity.read.fbo at sim res (default ~512x{aspect} = ~0.15M px, ~2.4MB Float32Array — cheap, do every sampled frame) and hash the raw buffer bytes (e.g. FNV-1a/xxhash over the Float32Array's Uint8Array view). Read density.read.fbo at full dye res (default ~2048x{aspect}, ~2.3M px, ~38MB) only at sparse checkpoints (e.g. frame 50/100/end). fp16 storage means values are already quantized — byte-exact buffer comparison is the correct bit-identity test (this is how the prior 0-mismatch verification worked).
hashRecipe.downsampledOption: No prebuilt GPU-downsample readback helper exists; if dye reads are too heavy, either CPU-stride-subsample like grain() does (js/08b-jank-monitor.js:371-372, stride 2) — fine for drift DETECTION but not proof of bit-identity — or blit density into an existing smaller RGBA16F FBO (e.g. shadeForm) and read that; only full-res reads prove bit-identity.
hashRecipe.noExistingHashCode: grep for hash/mismatch/bitIdentical found no in-repo hashing helper — harness must bring its own

Keep window size fixed and governor disabled during a run; window.velocity etc. are refreshed by exposeSimStats after a reinit.

consoleCapture.harnessRecipe: Capture via CDP: Runtime.enable + Runtime.consoleAPICalled + Runtime.exceptionThrown (and Log.enable/Log.entryAdded for network/GL driver messages). Alternatively chain window.onerror in an injected script BEFORE index.html's inline script would be needed to catch it first — index.html assigns window.onerror early, so an injected wrapper installed later can wrap the existing handler and push into a window.__testErrors array. The error card DOM is also queryable as a fallback signal.
